summary: Tested the Ask Pari Doubts fix (retry UX + /health) on preview. The DoubtsSession modal opens, both dashboard-pill and in-modal Pari avatars render correctly (pari_waving.png + pari_listening.png, 1024x1024, no broken image — the user's screenshot broken-image icon reproduces NEITHER on the pill nor inside the modal in this env). /api/health returns 200 {"status":"ok"} as before, and the backend /health route works on port 8001 directly (pod probe path — verified with localhost curl). However a CRITICAL REGRESSION was introduced by this fix: clicking the Send button (or, in offline test, sending any message) throws an uncaught 'TypeError: (intermediate value)(intermediate value)(intermediate value).trim is not a function' at bundle.js line matching DoubtsSession.jsx send() `const msg = (overrideMsg ?? input).trim();`. Because `send` is now attached as `onClick={send}`, React passes the click MouseEvent as first arg, so `overrideMsg = MouseEvent` and .trim() blows up. Result: happy-path send is BROKEN (no assistant reply), and offline path can't reach the new retry state either (retry button never renders). Root cause + one-line fix noted in action_items. Retry button test could not be completed end-to-end because the send() crash short-circuits everything.

minor.issue: Returns the frontend HTML (HTTP 200), NOT the backend {"status":"ok"} — because the platform ingress only forwards /api/* to :8001; /health hits the frontend at :3000. Pod liveness probe (which hits :8001 directly) DOES work — curl http://localhost:8001/health returns {"status":"ok"}. Not a bug but worth documenting: the review request's implied external-URL check of /health cannot actually reach the backend route in this environment.

ui_bugs.issue: REGRESSION FROM THIS FIX: `send = useCallback(async (overrideMsg) => { const msg = (overrideMsg ?? input).trim(); ... })` is passed directly as `onClick={send}` on the Send button (line ~408). React passes the MouseEvent as the first arg, so overrideMsg is a MouseEvent object, `(overrideMsg ?? input)` returns the event, and `.trim()` throws TypeError. Every click of the Send button now crashes with an Uncaught runtime error; no /api/doubts/start or /api/doubts/ask call is fired, no user or assistant bubble appears from the click path (Enter-key path is unaffected because the onKeyDown handler explicitly calls `send()` with no args).

Same shape as above — `retry` is defined as `useCallback(() => { if (lastFailedMsg) send(lastFailedMsg); })` which is fine, but `<button onClick={retry}>` also passes a MouseEvent → retry itself is fine (it doesn't touch the arg), and it then calls send(lastFailedMsg) with a string, so retry path would work IF a retry state could ever be reached. Given the send() crash above, retry state is currently unreachable via button-click. Enter-key send + retry SHOULD still work end-to-end (unverified — blocked by same crash on any subsequent Send button click).

integration_issues.issue: Send button click crashes before any network call; no assistant reply arrives; ChatBubble for the user's message DOES render (setMessages fires before .trim in the code, wait — actually setInput('') and setMessages(m => [...m, {role:'user', content: msg}]) come AFTER the .trim so they never run either). Screenshot 42 shows the modal with only the placeholder 'Ask me anything about this.' state and no bubbles after clicking Send.

integration_issues.flow: Ask Pari offline retry UX (the whole point of this fix)
integration_issues.issue: Could not be validated end-to-end. Because the Send-button click crashes with the .trim TypeError BEFORE fetch() runs, the try/catch never fires, `lastFailedMsg` never gets set, and the Retry button never renders. The new retry UX is currently DEAD CODE via the button click path. Enter-key submission may still exercise it correctly but was not testable because the first happy-path send has to succeed for a session to be provisioned before offline testing makes sense.

action_items: CRITICAL FIX in /app/frontend/src/components/tutor/DoubtsSession.jsx: The Send button and retry button pass a MouseEvent to `send`, which then does `(overrideMsg ?? input).trim()` and crashes. Change either the send handler signature or the button wiring. Simplest one-line fix on line ~148: `const send = useCallback(async (overrideMsg) => { const raw = typeof overrideMsg === 'string' ? overrideMsg : input; const msg = raw.trim(); ... }` OR change the button to `onClick={() => send()}` (line ~408) — same for the retry button `onClick={() => retry()}`. Recommend the signature guard (safer + future-proof).
Re-verify offline → Retry → online flow end-to-end after the fix; also verify Enter-key send still works (should already, but confirm).
Consider adding a smoke test that mounts DoubtsSession and clicks Send once — this would have caught the regression immediately.

(Optional) The external-URL /health probe cannot reach the new backend route because the ingress only forwards /api/*. If the RCA assumed external readiness probing, this fix only helps the pod-internal liveness path on :8001 (which does work). Confirm with platform team which probe path was 404'ing.
critical_code_review_comments: DoubtsSession.jsx line 148: `send = useCallback(async (overrideMsg) => { const msg = (overrideMsg ?? input).trim(); ... })` — the parameter should either be validated (typeof === 'string') or the callers should wrap: `onClick={() => send()}`. This is a classic React footgun.

The dependency array for `send` useCallback (line 258) omits `attemptContext` and a few other referenced values — ESLint disable line is in place but consider whether stale-closure behavior on those props is acceptable when the modal stays open across attemptContext updates.

AvatarPersona.jsx is unchanged and correctly resolves /tutor/pari_<pose>.png. No 404s observed for pari_waving, pari_listening, or pari_idle in this test. The broken-image icon reported by the user is not reproducible in the current preview build — likely a stale CDN/browser cache in the user's session or a transient pod-restart 404 (which is what this fix's /health addition is meant to prevent going forward).

Backend server.py root-level `@app.get('/health')` route is correctly defined and returns {"status":"ok"} when hit on :8001 directly. This is only useful for pod-internal probes — external traffic through the platform ingress still hits the frontend for /health. That's fine, just document.

rca of the issue: The fix added `send = useCallback(async (overrideMsg) => { const msg = (overrideMsg ?? input).trim(); ... })` and a new `retry` callback, but the Send button was left wired as `onClick={send}`. React's onClick invokes the handler with a synthetic MouseEvent as arg 0, so `overrideMsg` is that MouseEvent, `overrideMsg ?? input` returns the event (nullish-coalescing only defaults on null/undefined), and `.trim()` throws. Reproduction: open dashboard → click Pari pill → modal opens → type any 5+ char message → click Send button (NOT Enter key) → 'Uncaught runtime errors: TypeError: (intermediate value)(intermediate value)(intermediate value).trim is not a function' overlay appears; no user bubble, no /api/doubts/start call. Mitigation: change line ~408 to `onClick={() => send()}` and line ~364 to `onClick={() => retry()}`, OR guard inside send() with `const raw = typeof overrideMsg === 'string' ? overrideMsg : input;`.
